_meta.indication: Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.phase: Adequate and well-controlled (pivotal) trial; single trial supporting substantial evidence of effectiveness
pivotal_trials.design: 24-week multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 2:1 randomization to Cohort A (Q4W) or Cohort B (Q8W), and within each cohort 3:1 randomization to donidalorsen or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent patients (12 years and older) with HAE Type I or Type II
pivotal_trials.endpoint: The time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to Week 25 compared to placebo for donidalorsen 80 mg Q4W
pivotal_trials.n: 90 treated (planned 84; actually randomized 91); Q4W n=45, Q8W n=23, placebo n=22
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant reduction in HAE attacks per 4 weeks: donidalorsen-4 LS mean 0.44 vs placebo 2.26 (81% reduction, 95% CI 65%, 89%); donidalorsen-8 LS mean 1.02 (55% reduction, 95% CI 22%, 74%)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%): injection site reactions (24% Q4W), upper respiratory tract infection, urinary tract infection, abdominal discomfort. Anaphylaxis occurred in one subject; decreases in platelet count and increases in liver enzymes observed.
target_moa: GalNAc-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide that binds prekallikrein (PKK) mRNA, causing RNase H1-mediated degradation and reduced PKK production, thereby reducing downstream bradykinin, the main mediator of angioedema in HAE

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not held for this application; it did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues requiring external input.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation for the treatment of HAE, received September 19, 2023

citations.quote: On September 19, 2023, donidalorsen received orphan designation for the treatment of HAE.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA approved on the basis of a single adequate and well-controlled trial (CS5/OASIS-HAE) plus confirmatory mechanistic evidence; donidalorsen held orphan designation for HAE, and approval carried nonclinical and clinical postmarketing requirements.

citations.quote: Substantial evidence of effectiveness of donidalorsen in patients with HAE was established using data from a single adequate and well-controlled trial (CS5) studying two dosing regimens (80 mg every 4 weeks [Q4W] and 80 mg every 8 weeks [Q8W]) and placebo, and confirmatory evidence (CE) based on mechanistic data; see the description in Section 1.2.
